criteria.criterion: The query digest is sent in the system prompt and nowhere else: a recording-runner test over judge() shows it in a byte-identical system_prompt on every call and in ZERO instructions; checked by the new test in tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py.

Ordered-pair semantics are preserved in the payload: a test asserts the reference string is in the FIRST slot for ordering 1 and the SECOND slot for ordering 2, candidate block in the other; checked by the new ordering test.

citation.description: 4th ticket comment records 12/12 ordered pairs with identical relations (BEFORE->AFTER), per-pair breakdown with relation and confidence values, no relation changes, explicitly noting confidence moves within sampling variance.

criteria.criterion: Judgement precision is shown, not assumed: a real-API verdict-parity run over one query ticket and at least six candidate digests reports, per ordered pair, the baseline vs hoisted relation / shared_artifact / confidence, and is recorded as a ticket comment. Any pair whose relation differs is called out explicitly; identical relations on every pair is the pass condition.
The step stays advisory and fail-safe: with a runner that raises on every call, judge() returns [] and raises nothing; checked by the extended error test.
The default path is byte-identical: judge_one without the new keyword argument produces the same system_prompt and instructions as before; checked by the back-compat test.
